tools.name: init_core_memories
tools.description:
Run ONCE at conversation start. Loads behavioral prefs + recent context.

Previews carry a 'complete' flag: true = full content shown; false = opening only, memory_retrieve(id) for the rest.
After init, use memory_search for specific queries.
Shared collections -> 'collections' field. Pending teamma

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
Store a memory. Several memories in one call -> memories=[{content, topics, ...}]; top-level topics then apply to every item.

BEFORE params decide: (1) TYPE? (2) what search finds this later? (3) happened, or aspirational? (4) WHO must act on it?

TYPE by example:
  "User prefers dark mode" -> pref

tools.name: memory_add_batch
tools.description:
Store multiple memories at once. Same rules as memory_add, applied per item.

SHAPE: one ITEM here == one memory_add call. Same field names, same meaning. The ONLY
difference is the container: memory_add takes them as flat parameters, this takes a list
of objects. An item object belongs in the "memo

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description:
Search memories by relevance. Up to 32 results.

Query = ALL nouns from the user's message, not just the main one (ranking is automatic).
  "How does the app cache API calls?" -> "app cache api calls"
complete=false results are truncated -> memory_retrieve(id) for full content.
Auto-includes all you

tools.name: memory_deep_search
tools.description:
Broad search for a FULL sweep -- every hit on a topic (e.g. before memory_consolidate), not a conversational lookup (that is memory_search). Up to 128 results; requires 2+ keywords ("python" alone = too broad).

Scores: 30+ excellent, 20+ good, <20 weak.
Full sweep of a topic intersection. complete=

tools.name: memory_retrieve
tools.description:
Get full content by ID. Use when search returned complete=false.
Batch: memory_retrieve(["id1","id2"]). Skip if complete=true (preview is already full).

tools.name: artifact_write
tools.description:
Store or update a long document (markdown, JSON or text) behind a pointer memory. For agents.md, skills.md, assertions.md, a project plan: anything past one memory's 768-token cap.

CREATE: name ("assertions.md"), summary (the pointer memory: what the document is and why; search finds the pointer, n

tools.name: artifact_read
tools.description:
Read an artifact by its pointer memory id (memory_retrieve on a pointer shows an "artifact" block with head_rev_id and outline).
Bodies over 40,000 characters return the outline: read a section (heading path or JSON pointer) or page=0,1,... Returns rev_id; pass it as base_rev_id when you write.

tools.name: artifact_history
tools.description: List the revisions of an artifact (rev_id, parent, seq, time, author, pinned) and its heads. conflict=true means divergent heads to merge.

tools.name: artifact_pin
tools.description: Pin a revision so retention thinning never removes it (pinned=false unpins).

tools.name: artifact_delete
tools.description: Delete an artifact: every revision and its pointer memory. Permanent. confirm must equal the artifact name. memory_delete refuses a pointer; use this.

tools.name: artifact_orphans
tools.description: List artifact revisions whose pointer memory is gone (a delete on one replica racing a save on another). Nothing is auto-deleted; export includes them.

tools.name: memory_edit
tools.description:
Edit a memory. Provide only what changes; omitted fields untouched.

Modes:
1. Content replace (content [+topics/macro_topics]): full rewrite, re-embeds. Do it the instant the user corrects a memory ("actually...").
2. Metadata patch (topics/type/expiry, no content): type/expiry alone do not re-embe

tools.name: memory_delete
tools.description:
Delete memories by ID. Permanent.
memory_delete(["id1","id2"]). Delete by filter: memory_search first, collect ids, then delete.

tools.name: memory_consolidate
tools.description:
Create/replace a topic's executive summary. One per topic; replacing archives the old (restorable).

WARNING: a bad summary poisons every future session. Do NOT consolidate from partial knowledge.
BEFORE calling: (1) memory_deep_search the topic; (2) read 20+ memories, not previews; (3) if a summary

tools.name: task_feed
tools.description:
Recently-changed tasks, chronological (not ranked). For "what needs attention?" / "what changed?". Find tasks by content -> memory_search.

Each: preview, progress [done,total], status, topics, collection. Default 32, max 500.
Fan-out: no collection -> personal + all your collections.
Filters: statu

tools.name: collection_manage
tools.description:
Manage shared collections (multi-user memory folders).

list: your collections + invites. create. update: rename (display only; slug/keys unchanged).
delete: owner only, 2-step -- call without confirm to see impact + token, repeat with confirm:"<slug>". Permanent.
members: who's in it. add_user / re

tools.name: agent_manage
tools.description:
Manage agents (NAMESPACES under your account, sharing your token).

An agent is a namespace, never a holder of key material: all crypto is the
ACCOUNT's, and an agent id is never an input to a wrap, a seal or a KEK. Agents
organise and scope what is visible; they do not own encryption.

list. create

tools.name: signal
tools.description:
Inter-agent signals -- sticky notes pointing at a memory_id. Both parties must share a collection.

send: post to a teammate. check: read pending (removes nothing). ack: mark handled -- stamps delivered_at, the row stays, NOTHING IS DELETED.
ACK MEANS CLOSED, NOT DONE: it asserts only that no future

tools.name: message
tools.description: Direct inter-agent text that DIES ON ACK. Use for receipts, FYIs and short replies; use signal to point at a memory. send/check/ack. LOSABLE BY DESIGN: the first session of the recipient name to ack deletes it for every session of that name, an unacked message is deleted at expiry (default 7 days),

tools.name: account
tools.description:
Account state + billing. Returns URLs only -- user clicks to pay; never charges silently.

Pick by intent:
  "what plan am I on?" -> info (tier, subscription, capabilities, upgrade/downgrade SKUs; permanent tiers og/truebeliever/ogdev cannot downgrade)
  "what can I buy?" / "how much is Pro?" -> pla

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "gnosismemory.com" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: memory_add, memory_search, memory_edit, collection_manage, agent_manage, signal, message, account · Private data: artifact_write, memory_edit, collection_manage, agent_manage, account · Public sink: collection_manage, signal, message, account · Destructive: init_core_memories, memory_add, artifact_delete, artifact_orphans, memory_edit, memory_delete, collection_manage, agent_manage.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: memory_add, memory_search, memory_edit, collection_manage, agent_manage, signal, message, account · Private data: artifact_write, memory_edit, collection_manage, agent_manage, account · Public sink: collection_manage, signal, message, account · Destructive: init_core_memories, memory_add, artifact_delete, artifact_orphans, memory_edit, memory_delete, collection_manage, agent_manage

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
